title: Koszul perfect objects represent cohomology classes on a principal open
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], choose $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$, and put $U=D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_r)$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For $e\ge1$, let $K^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ be the cochain Koszul complex, and define $I^i(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)=K^{i-1}(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ for $i\le0$ and $0$ for $i>0$, with differential the negative of the Koszul differential. Let $I_e\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K_e\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the objects associated to these complexes; the canonical triangle is $I_e\xrightarrow{u_e}\mathcal O_X\to K_e\to I_e[1]$. The canonical comparison maps for powers give $I_1\leftarrow I_2\leftarrow\cdots$, compatible with the $u_e$. Then every $I_e$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], every $u_e|_U$ is an isomorphism, and the canonical map $\varinjlim_e\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(I_e,E)\to H^0(U,E|_U)$, sending $\varphi$ to $\varphi|_U\circ(u_e|_U)^{-1}$ under $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(\mathcal O_U,E|_U)=H^0(U,E|_U)$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For each e, the shifted Koszul complex I_e is perfect and its augmentation u_e restricts to an isomorphism on U, by the finite-free Koszul calculation and the contractibility after inverting one of the f_i.

The complexes I_e and maps u_e are functorial in e: the map from the complex on (f_1^{e+1},\ldots,f_r^{e+1}) to that on (f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e) multiplies the basis vector [i_0,\ldots,i_p] by f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}; the Koszul differential formula verifies that this is a chain map and that the augmentations commute. This gives the displayed inverse system.

By the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] (essential surjectivity) we may take $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ for a complex of $A$-modules $M^\bullet$; then $\mathcal F^\bullet=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ is a complex of quasi-coherent modules representing $E$ with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\bullet)=M^\bullet$, and $I_e=\widetilde{I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)}$. Apply the Koszul-Cech derived comparison [lem-sc-affine-koszul-cech-derived-comparison]: $\varinjlim_e\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(I^\bullet(f^e),M^\bullet)\to R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism; take $H^0$, which commutes with the filtered colimit, and note $H^0R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\bullet)=H^0(U,E|_U)$. $H^0\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(I^\bullet(f^e),M^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(I^\bullet(f^e),M^\bullet)$ by definition of the Hom complex, and this equals $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(I^\bullet(f^e),M^\bullet)$ because $I^\bullet(f^e)$ is a bounded complex of finite free (hence projective) modules, so K-projective [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], and Hom out of a K-projective complex in $K(A)$ equals Hom in $D(A)$ (Stacks, Derived Categories, Lemma derived-lemma-K-projective; $M^\bullet$ may be unbounded). By full faithfulness in [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(I^\bullet(f^e),M^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(I_e,E)$ ($D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ being a full subcategory). The composite identification is restriction to $U$ followed by $(u_e|_U)^{-1}$, so the canonical map is an isomorphism.

The restriction formula is well-defined on the colimit because the u_e commute with the transition maps. For r=0, U is empty and both sides are zero; for E=0 both sides are zero. These checks also agree with the stated canonical map.
